knowledge_gaps: Panel construction is underspecified: frequency-bin boundaries, zero-frequency handling, TF–IDF tokenization, vocabulary limits, title/description weighting, and catalog-to-metadata ID mapping need explicit definitions.

Lexical competitors may differ from uniform competitors in popularity and metadata completeness. Equal panel sizes alone cannot attribute rank changes specifically to lexical similarity; report these differences or add a frequency-controlled lexical contrast.

Requiring 99 positive-similarity lexical competitors can select unusually well-documented, common items. Report eligibility by category, target frequency, and history length, and distinguish common-row comparisons from panel-specific summaries.

A single frozen random panel gives reproducible but draw-dependent results. Predeclare whether bounded repeated candidate draws are needed, summarize within each history first, and avoid treating draws or repeated loader rows as independent users.

The proposal cannot directly measure compatibility, fulfilled needs, or willingness to choose now. Those qualitative failure modes require explicit evidence or feedback; difficult training-panel ranks do not establish recommendation errors or shortcut learning.

Implementation depends on a real-item mapping absent from the stated ModelView contract. Define a supported mapping source, device placement, empty-text behavior, nonfinite-score exclusions, identity-failure handling, and runtime limits within the shared budget.

The current code analysis describes no perturbation probes, while previous results describe extensive probes. Establish which implementation is being extended before promising to retain them. The unidentified SIGIR 2026 citation also requires verification.

Originality 4 is reasonable for methodological integration. Potential 7 is optimistic without evidence connecting training-panel findings to held-out improvement; difficulty 3 understates mapping, sparse retrieval, coverage auditing, and integration work.
